description:
A photographer brief that actually works has 6 components. Most briefs cover 2.

1. Event overview. What, where, how long.
2. Priority subjects. Named people and branded elements that must appear in the delivery.
3. Chronological shot list tied to the run of show.
4. Logistical constraints. Restricted zones, lighting conditions, timing limits.
5. Delivery specs. Format, resolution, turnaround, and who receives the files.
6. Usage context. Where each image set will appear. Composition decisions happen on the day.

A brief that covers all six produces a first delivery that requires no revision call.

When you brief a photographer, which of these do you usually leave out?
